_: Health Mirror. Every assertion here is mutation-controlled: health_mirror.py is a new standalone tool, never patched into existence, so there is no previous build to contrast it with and the version stage cannot apply. See NC_MIRROR.py. Mutation is the stronger control anyway -- it shows the assertion responds to the thing it claims to measure, not to a version change that moved several things at once. The five chosen are the promises the mirror actually makes: a missing stop date is stated rather than guessed, an unlogged meal day is not a zero, the sleep section never scores a night, a failed upload never marks the mirror fresh, and no molecule name reaches the tracked tool.

assertions.name: 03 a missing stop date is said, never invented

mutation.why: a medicine with no recorded stop date is given today's date instead of being marked unknown

assertions.name: 06 meal days are 'not logged' or 'partial', never a false zero

mutation.why: a day with nothing logged is written out as a day of zero intake

assertions.name: 05 the sleep section never scores a night

mutation.why: the sleep section starts grading the nights
mutation.find: A("apart. **No score, grade or good/poor label is given, here or anywhere.**")
mutation.replace: A("apart. Each night is given a sleep quality rating of good or poor.")

assertions.name: 11 a failed upload never marks the mirror fresh

mutation.why: the upload reports success when rclone was never configured, so a stale mirror looks current
mutation.find:
if not os.path.exists(conf):
        return False, "rclone has no configuration yet (the one sign-in is still to do)"

assertions.name: 12 no molecule name lives in the tracked tool

mutation.why: the night window is replaced by a hardcoded list of medicine names in tracked code
